data.taskBrief:
Look up an employee compensation-band lookup value in the Deel Local Payroll API (Deel Local Payroll API v2.0)

FIT
Fully. The supplied lookup request provides the capability needed to retrieve compensation/pay-rate lookup values. All supplied requests serve the task.

AUTH
Bearer token authentication for the request.
Header: Authorization: Bearer <payspace-access-token>
Also send the schema-specified header: content-type: application/json.

BASE URL
The request uses the unresolved {{api-base-url}} origin. The collection documentation lists staging and production API hosts, but does not resolve which one this request should use.

STEPS
1. GET /odata/v2.0/:company-id/Lookup/TableBuilderComponentCompany/:TableBuilderComponentCompany
   Params:
     company-id: string — '{{company-id}}'; place in the path.
     TableBuilderComponentCompany: string — '{{TableBuilderComponentCompany}}'; place in the path.
     frequency: string — '{{frequency}}'; place in the query string.
     period: string — '{{run}}'; place in the query string.
     $count: boolean — '{{ $count }}' as supplied by the request, or true/false; optional query parameter to request the total count.
     $filter: string — '{{ $filter }}' as supplied by the request; optional OData filter expression in the query string, such as "Action eq 'Deduction'".
   Returns:
     200 OK with an OData object containing @odata.context (string), @odata.count (number; example 1), and value (array) whose entries contain Value (string) and Description (string).
   Threading:
     None

GOTCHAS
- Replace {{api-base-url}}, {{payspace-access-token}}, {{company-id}}, {{TableBuilderComponentCompany}}, {{frequency}}, and {{run}} with actual values; the provided collection variables leave these placeholders unresolved.
- Keep company-id and TableBuilderComponentCompany in the path, not the query string; frequency and period are query parameters.
- Encode OData filter expressions correctly when using $filter.
- The collection documentation states that GET responses default to 100 records and support $skip/$top paging, but those parameters are not present in this request schema; do not add them unless the request is extended.
- Include User-Agent: payspace.com as required by the collection documentation.
- The saved example uses $count=true and returns one lookup entry; the request schema marks $count and $filter as optional.
- The request description mentions employee pay-rate information, while the saved response shows generic lookup Value and Description fields; inspect the returned values to identify the compensation-band entry.
